# Amber Lan · AI marketing engineer · AI marketing for New Zealand and Australia (flowai.co.nz)

> Amber Lan is an AI marketing engineer in Auckland, New Zealand. She builds the AI agents that run marketing for businesses in New Zealand and Australia (search, content, outbound and reporting) with your team, then hands them over. Flow AI is the trading name she uses for contract builds. This site is also her open portfolio: the AI agent systems that run a marketing function, built and documented in public. She is open to senior marketing engineer and GTM engineer roles, remote from anywhere.

Note: Flow AI (flowai.co.nz) is not affiliated with Flow Digital (flow.co.nz), Flow Marketing NZ, or the FLOWAI DISC-assessment product by Discflow.

Each build starts with a written scope and is priced per project. The team keeps running the system after a documented handover.

- /blog/: guides for owners and marketing leads in New Zealand and Australia, grouped by topic. Filter with /blog/?topic=<topic>.
- /glossary/: plain definitions of AI marketing and AI search terms, free to quote with attribution.
- Topic: AI search (/blog/?topic=ai-search). Getting found by Google and quoted by ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews.
  - /blog/what-is-answer-engine-optimisation [pillar]: Answer engine optimisation (AEO) is the work of making your business easy for AI answer engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI Overviews to find, understand and name in their answers. It builds on normal SEO: crawlable pages, clear facts, direct answers to real questions, and mentions of your business on other trusted sites.
  - /blog/aeo-checklist: An AEO checklist for a small business covers six areas: open your site to AI crawlers, publish consistent facts about the business, write pages that answer customer questions directly, earn reviews and mentions elsewhere, add accurate structured data, and track what AI engines say about you. Most owners can work through it in a week.
  - /blog/aeo-vs-seo-vs-geo: SEO gets your pages ranked in search results. AEO gets your business quoted or recommended inside the answers AI tools write. GEO is the research term for the same goal in generative AI engines such as ChatGPT and Perplexity. In practice AEO and GEO overlap almost completely, and both rest on good SEO.
  - /blog/get-recommended-by-chatgpt-auckland: Auckland businesses get recommended by ChatGPT and Google Maps when local facts about them are complete and agree everywhere. Set up your Google Business Profile with the right category and your suburbs as service areas, keep your name, address and phone identical everywhere including the NZBN register, collect recent reviews, and publish a page for each service and area.
  - /blog/how-to-get-mentioned-by-chatgpt: There is no form to submit your business to ChatGPT. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode and Copilot build answers from the open web and their search partners, so you get mentioned and recommended by being easy to find and confirm: crawlable pages that answer buyer questions, consistent business details, recent reviews, and mentions on sites the assistants already trust.
  - /blog/seo-for-small-business-nz: SEO for a New Zealand small business starts with Google, which handles about nine in ten NZ searches. Complete and maintain your Google Business Profile, collect recent reviews every week, give each service and each area you cover its own page, and fix the technical basics in Search Console. Most owners can do the first month themselves.
- Topic: Costs and choices (/blog/?topic=costs). What marketing help costs in New Zealand and Australia, and how to choose.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-cost-australia-new-zealand [pillar]: In 2026, AI marketing for a small business costs USD 20 to 99 a month per tool if you do the work yourself, NZD 60 to 150 an hour from a freelancer, NZD 1,500 to 10,000 a month from an agency, or NZD 90,000 to 130,000 a year for an in-house hire. AI marketing agents sit between the tool and the agency.
  - /blog/agency-vs-freelancer-vs-in-house: A freelancer is usually cheapest for New Zealand small businesses at NZD 50 to 150 an hour. An agency retainer costs NZD 1,500 to 10,000 a month for more than one channel, and an in-house marketer costs about NZD 76,000 to 167,000 a year once KiwiSaver and overheads are added. Ongoing workload decides which fits.
  - /blog/ai-advisory-pilot-nz: New Zealand's AI Advisory Pilot is a government grant, delivered through the Regional Business Partner Network, that pays up to 50% of eligible costs for expert AI help: up to $2,500 towards an AI roadmap and up to $12,500 towards implementation. Businesses need an NZBN and fewer than 50 full-time employees. It is open until 30 June 2027.
  - /blog/ai-agency-vs-ai-consultant-nz: Choose an AI marketing agency when you want marketing produced and run for you, an AI automation agency when a specific process wastes hours every week, and an AI consultant when you need a plan before you buy anything. If you have staff with time, an in-house person plus an outside engineer can cost less than all three.
  - /blog/ai-agent-development-cost-nz: Most of an AI agent's cost is people time. At the NZD 130 to 180 an hour Robert Walters lists for Auckland AI engineer contractors in 2026, a one-workflow agent taking three to five days costs about NZD 3,100 to 7,200 to build. Model and platform fees for a small agent can stay under NZD 100 a month.
  - /blog/ai-consultant-rates-nz-australia: AI consultants in Auckland charge about NZD 140 to 190 an hour on contract in 2026, according to Robert Walters, or roughly NZD 1,120 to 1,520 for an eight-hour day. In Australia, Hays puts AI engineer contractors at AUD 900 to 1,200 a day. Published fixed prices for small-business workshops and assessments start at NZD 795 plus GST.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-providers-australia: In October 2026, Australian AI marketing services came from five kinds of provider: AI-native agencies such as Flowterra Labs, established agencies adding AI such as Yoghurt Digital, AI search specialists such as Prosperity Media, automation firms such as Bolder Digital, and remote build-and-handover practices. Few publish prices, so compare what each shows and what you keep.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-providers-new-zealand: AI marketing services in New Zealand come from five kinds of provider: AI-native agencies such as Growin, established digital agencies that added AI such as Net Branding and Web Genius, AI search specialists such as The Optimisers and Pead, build-and-train firms such as AI Marketing NZ and King Tide, and marketing engineers, including this guide's publisher, Flow AI.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-scope-of-work: An AI marketing scope of work should state the business outcome and how it is measured, which agents and systems will be built, what data they can access, where a person reviews the work, the deliverables and who owns them, how handover and exit work, and the price with GST shown. Writing each point down now keeps both sides aligned later.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-services-vs-tools: Buy AI marketing tools when someone in the business has three or more hours a week and the skill to run one or two channels. Hire an AI marketing service when several channels must run and nobody has the time. Choose a build and handover when a team member has some hours and you want systems you own.
  - /blog/claude-vs-chatgpt-business-cost-nz: On their official pricing pages on 16 October 2026, Claude's Team plan and ChatGPT Business both cost US$20 per user per month billed annually, or US$25 billed monthly, with a two seat minimum. A 10 person team pays US$200 to US$250 a month before GST. Setup and staff training usually cost more than the seats.
  - /blog/do-you-need-an-ai-marketing-agency-nz: You need an AI marketing agency when marketing must run every week across more than one channel and nobody inside the business has the hours to run it. Check that the agency runs real AI systems you can see and keep. If you have the time or only one channel, a freelancer or AI tools may serve you better.
  - /blog/fractional-cmo-vs-ai-cmo: A fractional CMO is a senior marketer working part time, costing about NZD 4,000 to 10,000 a month in New Zealand and AUD 6,000 to 18,000 in Australia. An AI CMO is software that plans and often produces the work for far less. Choose the person for judgment and accountability, the software for weekly execution, or combine them.
  - /blog/fractional-marketing-manager-nz: A fractional marketing manager is an experienced marketer who works for your business part time, usually one or two days a week, owning the plan and the results without a full-time salary. Robert Walters' 2026 guide puts Auckland contract marketing managers at NZD 70 to 105 an hour, roughly NZD 2,450 to 3,700 a month for one day a week.
  - /blog/how-to-choose-an-ai-marketing-provider: Choose an AI marketing provider by asking for a run of its system on a real business, then asking who reviews the work, who owns the agents, accounts and data, how it meets the NZ or Australian Privacy Act, what it measures, what it costs in writing, and how you leave. Score each answer and pick the provider that shows the most.
  - /blog/how-to-hire-an-ai-agent-developer: Hire an AI agent developer by asking to see an agent they built running with its tests and logs, checking how they limit what the agent can read and do, and signing a contract that puts the code, prompts, accounts and data in your name, meets the Privacy Act and includes a written handover.
  - /blog/marketing-agency-alternatives-nz: The main alternatives to a marketing agency in New Zealand are doing it yourself with AI tools, a freelancer at NZD 50 to 150 an hour, a fractional marketing manager from about NZD 1,200 a month, a specialist package, an AI-led service, or an in-house hire on NZD 55,000 to 150,000 a year.
  - /blog/marketing-agency-cost-australia: Most Australian businesses pay a marketing agency AUD 2,000 to 6,000 a month in 2026. One channel such as SEO starts at about AUD 1,200 to 2,500, multi-channel growth work runs AUD 6,000 to 15,000, and agency hourly rates sit between AUD 80 and 350. Quotes usually exclude 10% GST and ad spend.
  - /blog/marketing-agency-cost-nz: Most New Zealand marketing agencies charge NZD 95 to 200 an hour. Monthly retainers run about NZD 500 to 1,500 for one channel, NZD 1,500 to 4,000 for several, and NZD 4,000 to 10,000 or more for full service, plus GST and ad spend. From NZD 1,000 a month, an agency has room to do one channel properly.
  - /blog/what-do-ai-marketing-services-include: AI marketing services cover the marketing jobs a provider runs on AI systems: positioning, AI search and SEO, content, social, outbound, conversion, paid media checks, community and reporting. Each line should name what it delivers each month and who approves it. You still own the strategy, the claims, the budget and every customer conversation.
- Topic: The AI marketing agent (/blog/?topic=agent). What an AI marketing agent is, what it does, and where the human sits.
  - /blog/what-is-an-ai-marketing-agent [pillar]: An AI marketing agent is software that reads your business, decides what marketing to do next, produces the work across several channels and ships it under a human's review. A tool waits to be prompted one task at a time. An agent holds a goal, chooses its next task and reports what changed.
  - /blog/ai-agents-for-marketing: Build a positioning brief first, because every marketing agent is briefed from it. Then build the agent for the gap that costs you most, usually search or outbound for a 5 to 50 person business. Install one agent at a time, give it narrow data access, put a human review before anything reaches a customer, and measure enquiries.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-automation-small-business: AI marketing automation is software that runs marketing steps on triggers, such as a welcome email after a sign-up, with AI writing, sorting and personalising the content inside each step. A small business should start with six: a welcome sequence, enquiry follow-up, quote follow-up, review requests, abandoned bookings or carts, and re-engagement.
  - /blog/claude-code-for-marketing-agencies: Start with a brief file for each client, then build research packs, first drafts, an SEO and AEO audit and monthly reporting, in that order. Keep each client in its own folder with its own connectors, put a person on review before the client sees anything, and use a commercial plan so client data stays out of model training.
  - /blog/n8n-vs-zapier-vs-make-vs-claude-code: Choose Zapier when non-technical staff need simple app-to-app automations quickly. Choose Make for visual multi-step scenarios at a lower entry price. Choose n8n when someone technical wants self-hosting or high volumes billed per run. Choose Claude Code when the work needs judgement, such as drafting a weekly report, and someone is comfortable working with files.
  - /blog/running-marketing-on-claude-code: You give each lane of marketing work its own instruction file, turn every repeated procedure into a versioned skill, connect the agent to the tools where marketing lives through MCP, and schedule the recurring briefs. The agents research and draft. One person reviews everything and approves what ships, so the judgement stays human.
  - /blog/what-is-a-marketing-engineer: A marketing engineer is a marketer who builds and runs the AI systems that produce a company's marketing, such as agents for search, content and reporting, and keeps the judgement over what ships. A GTM engineer builds the systems that feed sales: prospect lists, enrichment, sequencing and CRM automation. Either way, a real one can show you a running system.
  - /blog/what-is-an-ai-cmo: An AI CMO is software that does the planning half of a chief marketing officer's job. It reads the business and its market, sets priorities, writes the marketing plan, briefs the work and reviews the results each cycle. A human still owns positioning, pricing, claims, spend and anything that reaches a customer.
- Topic: Transformation (/blog/?topic=transformation). Moving a small business marketing function onto AI systems, job by job.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-transformation-small-business [pillar]: AI marketing transformation for a small business is the move from marketing done in spare hours to marketing run by systems, one job at a time. A practical 90-day path fixes positioning and measurement first, then search and content, then social and outbound, with a human approving everything that reaches a customer.
  - /blog/ai-for-marketers: Hand AI the production work of marketing: research, first drafts, repurposing, scheduling, tracking and follow-up. Keep the judgment: positioning, the claim worth making, taste, the call on what ships and conversations with buyers. Put a named person and a short review step between every AI draft and the customer, and measure hours saved alongside enquiries.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-examples: Ten practical AI marketing examples for a small business, one per marketing job: a positioning file, AI search answer pages, a weekly guide, one social channel, researched outbound, quote follow-up, a launch kit, review replies, a weekly ad check and a one-screen report. In each, AI drafts the work and a named person approves it.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-for-small-business-nz: AI marketing for a New Zealand small business covers four systems: SEO so Google finds you, answer engine optimisation so ChatGPT and AI search quote you, a content engine that publishes every week, and outbound follow-up that never forgets. Most businesses start with one system, prove it, then add the next.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-privacy-law-nz-australia: Yes, if the provider takes only the data each job needs, keeps personal information out of AI tools that retain or train on it, signs a contract limiting use to your purposes, and tells you where the data is processed. In New Zealand and Australia your business stays responsible for that data, including when an AI vendor processes it offshore.
  - /blog/ai-marketing-strategy-small-business: Build an AI marketing strategy in five steps: write your positioning and the questions customers ask, hand one or two marketing jobs to AI first, set rules for what a person approves, choose two numbers to measure, and run it for 90 days. Keep it to one page and review it monthly.
  - /blog/content-marketing-small-business-nz: Content marketing for a New Zealand small business means publishing useful answers to the questions your customers already ask, on a schedule you can keep. Write one solid piece a fortnight, cut it into social posts, an email and FAQ entries, and check enquiries monthly. Two to four hours a week is enough to start.
  - /blog/first-month-of-an-ai-marketing-build: A well-run AI marketing build spends week one on a written scope and positioning brief, week two installing the first agent with a person approving its output, week three running it against a baseline, and week four on handover documents and choosing the next agent. You provide access, decisions and one to two hours of review each week.
  - /blog/outbound-sales-automation: Outbound sales automation for a small business means using software and AI to build a target list, research each account, draft short personal emails and send follow-ups on a schedule, while a person approves every first message and handles every reply. In New Zealand and Australia it must also meet spam law on consent, identification and unsubscribing.

## What is an AI marketing engineer?

An AI marketing engineer does two jobs that are usually split: they write the go-to-market strategy, and they build the AI systems that execute it. One person designs the positioning and ships the inbound, content, and outbound systems that run it. Flow AI's practitioner rule: claims ship with receipts. The systems are public on GitHub, and client results are only published with real names and real numbers.

## What does AI marketing cost in New Zealand and Australia?

Flow AI prices each build per project once a written scope is agreed, and does not publish prices. Sourced market ranges for tools, freelancers, agencies and in-house hires in both countries: https://www.flowai.co.nz/blog/ai-marketing-cost-australia-new-zealand
